summary.headline: Coromandel Q2 FY27: EBITDA fell 18% to ₹944 crore on NPK margin compression, while revenue rose 6% to ₹10,348 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 was hit by deficient monsoon rainfall in key states, a roughly 40% industry-wide fall in NPK production and consumption, high raw material (sulphur, ammonia) costs and thin NBS rates. Coromandel cut primary sales about 30% and production 15% to 7.7 lakh tonnes to manage working capital, while lifting its market share from 17% to 19%. Crop protection revenue rose 22%, but NACL's EBITDA fell sharply on high-cost carryover inventory. Management said the new NBS rates for the Rabi 2026-27 season were approved the previous day and should support MRP correction and NPK volume recovery, though it is still awaiting the detailed notification.

segments.name: Nutrients (NPK / DAP / SSP)
segments.commentary: Primary sales fell about 30% and consumption about 33%, with production cut 15% to 7.7 lakh tonnes. Market share rose from 17% to 19%. SSP volumes fell 13% to 1.9 lakh tonnes.

segments.name: Crop protection
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22%, driven by export markets, which were about 45% of revenue. Domestic demand stayed soft, and six new products were launched across agrochemicals and biologics.

segments.name: NACL (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue was ₹374 crore, down 18%, and EBITDA was ₹12 crore, sharply lower on carryover high-cost inventory and falling prices for certain molecules.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Network grew by 80 stores in Q2 to 1,300 stores across five states, with a target of 2,000 in two years. Retail white-label brands are expected to cross ₹100 crore annual sales this year.

segments.name: Non-subsidy businesses (retail, specialty nutrients, bio, SSP)
segments.commentary: Management said these grew strongly and drove EBITDA despite the NACL drag, although non-subsidy sales in UP and Maharashtra were hit by state bans on non-substitutable fertilisers.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Rabi MRP corrections of at least 10-15% for NP/NPK grades, subject to the detailed NBS notification and the subsidy offsetting negative margins.
Backward-integration (phosphoric acid) spread is expected to improve in H2 as the Kakinada plant returns to full capacity from October; management called ~$350/t a safe assumption.
Grassroots granulation plant in Kakinada is targeted for commissioning by February 2027, with the capacity usable in the next season.
Management expects consumption and channel inventory to normalise by year-end, with NPK share recovering toward the historical mix.
Sulphur prices are expected to soften toward $900/t, with a possibility of falling below $500/t if purchases stay smart; DAP was rolled over at $700/t, and phosphoric acid prices held at $1,700/t.
Management said it is cautiously optimistic about Rabi, but expects some time before NACL's margins recover.
capex_capacity: Kakinada sulphuric acid and phosphoric acid plant was commissioned in Q2 and ran at reduced rates until sulphur supply resumed in August; it is now operating at full capacity.
Greenfield granulation plant in Kakinada is due for commissioning by February 2027, with ~₹2,000 crore invested in the phosphoric acid plant.
A flow-chemistry launch plant is being set up, with a possible commercial plant costing ₹200-300 crore in 1-2 years, subject to customer sign-ups.
A capacity expansion of one key agrochemical molecule was announced, planned for this month.
Mining operations at Senegal are being scaled up, and management said it will not go to 100% captive raw material supply.
demand_pricing: Industry-wide NPK production and consumption fell about 40% in Q2 as the DAP-NPK price gap pushed farmers toward DAP.
Industry NPK sales for H1 were about 60 lakh tonnes vs 121 lakh tonnes last year (management's figures); DAP was about 44 lakh tonnes.
Management said the DAP-NPK mix moved from about 60:40 to 30:70, and expects it to normalise with the new NBS rates.
Channel inventory is estimated at 5-7% above last year, and management expects it to fall by year-end.
Nano DAP is the market leader, with growing exports and registrations under way in Latin America, the Middle East and South Asia, but state bans have constrained sales.
Crop protection demand was soft domestically; export growth was about 44% standalone, with customers deferring purchases over crude-linked intermediates.

qa_highlights.question: How much MRP reduction is expected after the subsidy increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a minimum 10-15% moderation in NP/NPK grades (e.g., 20-20-0-13 rose from ₹1,350 to ₹2,100 per bag), subject to the notification and ammonia price movements.

qa_highlights.question: How much sulphur subsidy is included in Q2 results?
qa_highlights.answer: The subsidy applies only to shipments above a $800/t sulphur price threshold; management said the amount was not significant but helped in August and September.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-subsidy EBITDA rise while subsidy EBITDA fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Crop protection margins were hit by carryover high-cost inventory, but retail, specialty nutrients and SSP performed well. State bans on non-substitutable fertilisers in UP and Maharashtra are a temporary drag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for backward-integration spreads and the ~$350/t assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads are expected to improve from October onwards as Kakinada ramps up; management said ~$350/t is a safe assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new Kakinada granulation capacity fully utilised next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets full utilisation next year, with new NPK grades such as boron and zinc, and noted the NBS framework now allows innovation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for NACL and the flow chemistry business?
qa_highlights.answer: NACL margins should recover over 2-3 years as new registrations come through. The flow-chemistry launch plant is being set up, with commercial capex of ₹200-300 crore only once customers are signed up.

risks_watch: Whether the detailed NBS notification and MRP corrections are implemented, and their effect on NPK volumes in Rabi.
Monsoon deficit (20-30% in key states) and the slow recovery in agricultural acreage.
State restrictions on non-substitutable fertiliser sales in UP and Maharashtra, which hit nano and non-subsidy volumes.
NACL's margin recovery, given high-cost inventory and price pressure on older generic molecules.
Framework for fertiliser sales (pilot): a longer purchase process and the risk of constraints on NPK availability for farmers.
Subsidy receivables rose to ₹3,535 crore from ₹3,199 crore a year earlier.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management acknowledged an unprecedentedly challenging quarter but pointed to the new NBS rates, moderating raw material prices and better Rabi prospects. Management was evasive on specific Rabi margin and MRP numbers, saying it would wait for the notification and the quarter to close.
key_quotes: Q2 was the unprecedentedly challenging quarter for the industry.
I am happy to note that government yesterday announced the NBS rate for Abhi 26-27 season.

Once we have a visibility on the product getting cleared with key players, we should be able to set up a commercial plant which may involve capex of both 2-300 cores, probably 1-2 years down the line.

adds.what: Retail store network expansion to 2,000 stores (from 1,300)
Flow-chemistry commercial plant (possible, subject to customer sign-ups)

growth.why: Management guides Rabi MRP corrections of 10-15% and H2 phosphoric acid spread recovery, backed by Kakinada granulation (Feb 2027) and a 2,000-store retail target in two years, but NPK volumes fell ~40% industry-wide, NACL recovery is pushed out and no revenue growth number is guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides Rabi MRP corrections of at least 10-15% for NP/NPK grades and phosphoric acid spreads improving from October at a ~$350/t assumption, though Q2 EBITDA fell 18% to ₹944 crore and NACL recovery is pushed out.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kakinada greenfield granulation plant is under construction with commissioning targeted by February 2027, after ~₹2,000 crore invested in phosphoric acid and the sulphuric/phosphoric plant already running at full capacity since August.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects NPK consumption and channel inventory (5-7% above last year) to normalise by year-end after NPK volumes fell about 40% industry-wide and Coromandel cut production 15% to 7.7 lakh tonnes, though no volume number is guided.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Production was cut 15% on softer demand, so utilisation is falling rather than tight; the flow-chemistry commercial plant (₹200-300 crore) is contingent on customer sign-ups, and a one-molecule agrochemical capacity expansion was announced for this month.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was evasive on Rabi margin and MRP numbers and said it would wait for the NBS notification and quarter close, while H1 EBITDA fell 12% to ₹1,705 crore and NACL margins will take time to recover.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance depends on the detailed NBS notification and subsidy offsetting negative margins, state bans in UP and Maharashtra are constraining non-subsidy sales, and NACL recovery is pushed out with no numeric EBITDA path.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Six new crop protection products were launched in Q2, and management plans new NPK grades such as boron and zinc for the new granulation capacity, with retail white-label brands expected to cross ₹100 crore this year.

rows.label: Rabi NBS-driven MRP correction of 10-15%
rows.why: Management expects a minimum 10-15% moderation in NP/NPK grade MRPs (e.g., 20-20-0-13 from ₹1,350 to ₹2,100 per bag), subject to the detailed NBS notification and ammonia prices.

rows.label: Retail network expansion to 2,000 stores
rows.why: Network grew by 80 stores in Q2 to 1,300 across five states, with a stated target of 2,000 stores in two years.

rows.label: Subsidy receivables build-up
rows.why: Subsidy outstanding rose to ₹3,535 crore from ₹3,199 crore a year earlier, which ties up working capital even as sales volumes were cut to manage it.

tone.note: Management was cautiously optimistic on the new NBS rates, sulphur softening and Kakinada ramp-up, but was evasive on Rabi margin and MRP numbers and on the NACL recovery timeline; analysts pressed on the notification, MRP quantum and subsidy offsets.
